Heads up: I plan to add releases to the arena (called rounds) that are frozen, published as github releases and on zenodo, and linked from an index. (https://github.com/leanprover/lean-kernel-arena/pull/169)

I expect to do these releases not more often than quarterly or so, but not by a fixed schedule.

Probably the ongoing round will run until things settle (e.g. no new soundness bugs for a while so that everyone has a chance to fix them), and will avoid disruptive test-side changes like mathlib bumps. If it looks like things are settled I’ll probably give a one week warning here before cutting the release.

Mathlib updates that upset the results and expecially bumps that involved changes to the export format or the kernel logic will be done after closing a round and starting a new one.

New rounds will probably start with some checkers kicked out by me that look stale or unmaintained, so that we don’t carry one-off vibe coded projects for too long; of course re-adding them is fine.

Thoughts and concerns about that?

Ok, the infrastructure for this seems to work. So I'd like to announce the end of the current round: I will cut the round 2026-09 not before Mondays Sept 14.

It may happen later if new soundness bugs or other worthwhile tests appear to give people time to update.

It may also happen later for expected but hard to schedule real live events awaiting me :-)

We may make some tests expext: either, Mario asked for that so that lean4lean's divergent behavior about which projections exists is not penalized.
This is about to land (https://github.com/leanprover/lean-kernel-arena/pull/171)

Any other changes we really should do before that?
I'll cut the round more likely near the end of September, as some checker authors are on vacation right now. I assume there is no rush.

I added con-leche also as a test, but it broke a few checkers, presumably because it is from a newer toolchain (did not yet investigate)? That wasn't quite the promise for the round, so unless all affected checkers happen to catch up, I'll probably remove the test before cutting the round and add it back later .

The reason this test breaks some tests seems to be that it really needs a defeq shortcut at different binder depths, and for example nanobruijn doesn't do that easily. So it's a valid test case for real checkers, but still not nice to add it so late in the round.

eink0rn passes it, but for some reason spikes up to massive RAM, way more than anything in Mathlib. Something about the way that deeply nested match statements reduce. (Mathlib actually does relatively little with inductives, in that sense...) Trying to understand it better.

Mathgraph also fell over it, for yet another reason:
https://github.com/leanprover/lean-kernel-arena/pull/183#issuecomment-5630992312

It seems that this is a particular fruitful test to improve checker implementations :-)

It seems that all affected and actively maintained checkers have received fixes that allow them to handle the con-leche test case, so I’ll keep it around for the current round.

Tentative release date Sept 20.

Is anyone about to push something or should I press the button? (I'm still improving con-*, but may take more than a day or two to land the next changes, so it's probably not proper to wait for that.)
@Chris Emery do you want to get https://github.com/corun1024/lazylean into the arena in time for this round?
Just making a PR, if I'm not too late.
I did some more optimisations last day or so. It should be one of the fastest I think.

The first Lean Kernel Arena round is now released:
https://arena.lean-lang.org/round/2026-09/

It has a doi: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22944094.

Artifacts on https://zenodo.org/records/22944094 and also on https://github.com/leanprover/lean-kernel-arena/releases/tag/round-2026-09

Also see the “rounds” section of the collapsed details.

Congratulations all.. this has been a lot of fun. I’ve esoecially enjoyed learning from (and duelling with!) sokonanoda in the Arena :duel:

For Round 2, we have started a ground up, first-principles, and verification-first rewrite of MathGraph.. I am aiming for a much smaller independent kernel with optimisations that have to preserve independently checked semantics..

Really like the frozen, DOI-backed round format. It makes the Arena much more useful as a reproducible scientific benchmark, not just a moving leaderboard. And allows for a little break between rounds! Glad con-leche stayed in because it found real implementation weaknesses and made several checkers better. Thanks for putting this together @Joachim Breitner ! Looking forward to watching the arena evolve as the checkers get even better. See you in Round 2
